input: Masullo conditional for the relevant finite-order narrow-ray-class Hecke characters; Alpöge suffices when K=Q
status: classical with exact locator; random walks remain randomized and n,B are fixed in the mixing conclusion
where_the_proof_is: Jao–Miller–Venkatesan2009 Theorem1.1 authorp3, Remark1.2(a)/Cor1.3 p4, proofs pp7–10
where_it_lives: GRH_NIGHT.tex, complexity section; quantitative mixing input behind CX_GRH CX-N12/CX-ALG-019; arithmetic Picard correspondences SGA4 IXTheorem3.3; cote2 scan5

statement: For imaginary quadratic K, the genus quotient Cl(O_K)/Cl(O_K)^2 satisfies the small-prime spectral/mixing conclusions CX-ALG-020 under A_D alone. Its Hecke characters factor as products of rational Dirichlet L-functions through the abelian genus field. If Cl(O_K) has exponent two this covers its entire graph. Prime ideals of prime norm≤(8log|D_K|+15)² generate this quotient under A_D, using a degree-four class field for each nontrivial character.
input: Alpöge; classical class field theory and JMV character-by-character estimates; no M input
status: proved here as a precise quotient-level input refinement
where_the_proof_is: GRH_NIGHT.tex CX-ALG-021 full generalized-dihedral/genus-field/character proof; JMV2009 Remark1.2(a) p4 and proof of Theorem1.1 p9; Bach–Sorenson Theorem5.1 p1729 for the explicit quotient generator bound
where_it_lives: GRH_NIGHT.tex, complexity section; sharpens CX-ALG-013 and inherited CX_GRH CX-N07–N12 hypothesis split; Picard quotient, SGA4 IXTheorem3.3; cote2 scan5

statement: For ordinary elliptic curves over a fixed Fq with fixed point count and the same geometric endomorphism order, prime-degree isogenies below (log(4q))^B, B>2, form the cited expanding graph under M. A solver for discrete logarithms on a fraction μ of that level transfers to every curve on it with expected μ^{-1}poly(log q) overhead; no solver is supplied by this theorem.
input: Masullo conditional; imaginary-quadratic ring-class Hecke input, ordinary/same-level promise, and an independently supplied solver for the reduction conclusion
status: classical with exact locator, conditional on M; randomness retained
where_the_proof_is: JMV2009 Theorem1.5 authorp5; Theorem1.6 pp6–7; Proposition3.1 p11, Theorem3.3 p12, proofs pp12–14
where_it_lives: GRH_NIGHT.tex, complexity section; ORDER20 elliptic/abelian-variety programme; CM ideal-class action and finite isogeny correspondences; cote2 scan5 Picard companion

statement: For distinct primes p,r, an explicit F_{p^r} and a maximal equivariant Teichmüller unit in Fp[ζr] are polynomial-time interconstructible. The unit has exact order r^{v_r(p^{ord_r(p)}−1)}. A supplied F_{p^m} therefore supplies it unconditionally whenever r|m, even in the higher-valuation branch. Geometric form: a Kummer cover followed by finite étale descent.
input: neither; supplied prime-degree field or coefficient unit; supplied field degree m is charged to input size
status: classical equivalence with exact locator; new application to the prior finite-field gate proved here in full
where_the_proof_is: Lenstra1991 Theorems5.1–5.2 pp338–340, Theorem3.1 pp334–336; GRH_NIGHT.tex CX-ALG-023 complete normal-basis/product-projection and invariant-field proof
where_it_lives: GRH_NIGHT.tex, complexity section; strictly extends CX_GRH CX-N14/CX-U02 cases; SGA1 V§7, SGA4 IX3.2; inherited group-action companion cote28 scan3

statement: For odd prime r≠p, A_D makes RH for ζ_{Q(p^{1/r})} equivalent to RH for ζ_{Q(ζr,p^{1/r})}, via ζ_E=ζ_{Q(ζr)}(ζ_{Q(p^{1/r})}/ζ_Q)^{r−1}. It supplies q≡1 mod r with p^{(q−1)/r}≠1 mod q and q≤[4r(2r−3)log r+4(r−1)²log p+2.5r(r−1)+5]², hence an explicit F_{p^r} in poly(r log p).
input: Alpöge plus RH for one pure degree-r Dedekind zeta; Masullo supplies that extra input conditionally
status: proved here: exact permutation-character reduction and explicit discriminant/prime bound; field algorithm classical
where_the_proof_is: GRH_NIGHT.tex CX-ALG-024 full proof; Bach–Sorenson1996 Theorem5.1 p1729 and §2p1720; Adleman–Lenstra1986 AlgorithmA pp350–351, Lemma6 p352
where_it_lives: GRH_NIGHT.tex, complexity section; strict analytic-family refinement of CX_GRH CX-N11–N15; Artin finite-cover identity, SGA1 V§7; representation-ring companion SGA6 V§§2,7

statement: Degree-d factoring over supplied F_{p^m} remains deterministic quasipolynomial under A_D plus RH only for pure fields Q(p^{1/r}), r≤d prime with r∤(p−1)m and v_r(p^{ord_r(p)}−1)>1. Only actually encountered such r are needed. If no such r exist it is A_D-only; p≤d is unconditional polynomial. If every prime r≤d divides m or has valuation one, the quasipolynomial bound is unconditional. Geometric form: primitive-idempotent computation in the Frobenius-fixed split finite étale algebra.
input: Alpöge plus the displayed finite pure-prime-degree zeta family; Masullo supplies it conditionally; no additional analytic input when the family is empty
status: proved here as a new complete composition and strictly smaller sufficient gate; bound (d^{log d} log(p^m))^{O(1)} retained
where_the_proof_is: GRH_NIGHT.tex CX-ALG-025 full proof; CX-ALG-023/024; IKRS published authorPDF Theorem5.8 pp28–29, Proposition4.6 pp18–19, Lemma4.2 p16
where_it_lives: GRH_NIGHT.tex, complexity section; moves CX_GRH CX-U02 and refines CX-N15 from ν≤d² Kummer fields to pure prime degrees≤d; ORDER28; SGA1 V§7 and SGA4 IX3.2

statement: An explicit degree-n extension of supplied F_{p^m} is constructible in poly(n log(p^m)) from A_D and RH for pure Q(p^{1/r}) only at prime divisors r|n not covered by r=p, r|m, r|p−1 or valuation one. If every prime divisor r of n divides pm or has r≠p and valuation one, no analytic hypothesis is needed. In particular primes supported on pm suffice unconditionally. Geometric form: construct a connected degree-n finite étale cover.
input: Alpöge plus the displayed finite pure-prime-degree zeta family, conditionally supplied by Masullo; n unary or equivalent dense-output encoding
status: proved here as a complete input refinement of a classical field-construction theorem
where_the_proof_is: GRH_NIGHT.tex CX-ALG-026 full transfer proof; Lenstra1991 Theorem9.1 pp344–346, Theorem7.1 p342 and Theorem1.1 p330; CX-ALG-023/024
